phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: Three levels: formal (-mnida / -seumnida): news, business, meeting strangers. Polite (-yo): everyday, shops, adults you do not know well. Informal (drop the -yo): close friends of the same age, younger people, children. Use -yo when unsure.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Korean often drops pronouns. For "you" it is better to use the person's name or title + -ssi, because "dangsin" can sound rude or intimate.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Korean usually does not mark the plural. Add -deul to show "many" (chingu → chingudeul). Numbers and context show how many.

grammar.title: Ida: to be
text: "Ieyo" after a consonant, "yeyo" after a vowel.

grammar.title: Itda: to have, to exist
text: "Isseoyo" = there is / I have. "Eopseoyo" = there is not / I do not have.

grammar.title: Regular verbs (present tense)
text: Take the verb stem (drop -da), add -ayo or -eoyo (a / o vowel → -ayo, other vowels → -eoyo). Gada (go) → gayo, meokda (eat) → meogeoyo. Hada becomes haeyo.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Word order is subject, object, verb (verb last). Particles mark roles: -eun/-neun (topic), -i/-ga (subject), -eul/-reul (object).
ex: we live in a big house

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put an before the verb (short form) or add -ji anayo to the stem (long form). Never use "an" with "isseoyo": use "eopseoyo".
Put an before the verb (short form) or add -ji anayo to the stem (long form). For "there is not" use eopseoyo; for "is not" use ani-eyo.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: A yes / no question has the same words as a statement, with rising voice. No question word is needed.

grammar.title: Possessives
text: Use the pronoun + -ui, often shortened. Je = my (polite), nae = my (informal).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: Add -nim (title) to teachers and elders. Use -ssi after a name for equals: Minsu-ssi. Do not use -ssi to older people. Always speak politely to adults.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: stem + -ass/-eoss + eoyo. Future: stem + -l geoyeyo.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Polite command: stem + -(eu)seyo (oseyo = come, anjeuseyo = sit). Negative: stem + -ji maseyo (oji maseyo = do not come). Informal: stem + -eo / -a.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: -l su isseoyo = can (hal su isseoyo), -l su eopseoyo = cannot, -eoya haeyo = must (gaya haeyo), -go sipeoyo = want to (meokgo sipeoyo). Must not = -myeon an dwaeyo.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: -e = at / in / to (hakgyo-e), -eseo = at / in (for actions: hakgyo-eseo gongbuhaeyo). wi = top, ap = front, mit = under, yeop = beside, gakkai = near.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: deo = more (deo keoyo), gajang = the most (gajang keoyo). "Than" = -boda: ju-boda (than me). joa → deo joayo (better).
